SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Oral Literature 4.1.1 Short Forms of Oral Literature, part of SHORT FORMS OF ORAL LITERATURE Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Sugg in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How do the short forms of oral literature help in enhancing creativity and imagination?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Oral Literature 4.1.1 Short Forms of Oral Literature together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: This is enhanced as learner work with peers to compose, review and perform

short forms of oral literature.

● Citizenship: This is developed as the learner engages with others to discuss various aspects of short forms of oral

literature.

Values:
● Social justice: This is enhanced as the learner harmoniously interacts with peers to compose, review and perform short

forms of oral literature,

● Integrity: This is fostered as the learner chooses to practise self-discipline during the discussion, creation and

performance of short forms of oral literature.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: This is enhanced as the learner collaborates with others during discussions to create the short forms of oral

literature.
